subject: Urgent: Zenbridge production latency spike — provisional traffic siphon & stitch plan
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@zenbridge.io>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@zenbridge.io>, Zenbridge SRE <sre@zenbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting requests (region: us-east-1)

Irene / Redwood team —

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and 5xx errors starting ~09:00 PDT. Key customer journeys (search -> ranking) are timing out and several downstream services are seeing retry amplification. Sample metrics: 99th latency jumped from 320ms -> 2.1s; 5xx rate ~6% across us-east-1. Token generation queue backlog visible in our telemetry.

We've attached a small set of request traces and logs (zenbridge_error_logs_20270609.zip). This is user-impacting; can you confirm receipt and share next steps?

Alex Mercer
Sr. Platform Engineer | Zenbridge
alex.mercer@zenbridge.io

Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting requests (region: us-east-1)

Alex — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. We have the files and are kicking off an ops bridge.

Immediate plan (T-0):
- I will open the bridge and lead the initial triage.
- Short-term mitigation: propose an emergency traffic siphon of a portion of your production traffic from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 (read-only routing for non-stateful queries) to reduce pressure while we investigate.
- Fallback: if model inference latency is the root cause, we can temporarily route to our quantized v2 model (8-bit) for the busiest routes — small quality delta, large latency wins.

Can your SRE team accept a controlled siphon (10-25% initially) and confirm if any IP allowlists or regional compliance blockers exist? If yes, list immediately.

I'm looping in Priyom (CSM) and David (Infra lead). I'll post the bridge link in Slack in 2 minutes.

Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@zenbridge.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting requests (region: us-east-1)

Bridge summary and technical plan (current status: ongoing triage) —

Observations from initial triage:
- Inference host-side CPU and GPU utilization on the us-east-1 pool spiked simultaneously with backlog increases; memory KPIs show KV cache churn on the hot prefix space for Zenbridge routes.
- Error patterns point to a mixture of transient OOM-like GC events in the pre/post processing layer and a growing queue at the serving front-door.

Proposed immediate mitigation (executing on approval):
1) Controlled siphon: shift 15% of production traffic to us-west-2 via policy-based routing. This only affects stateless text-generation calls and is safe for search ranking queries. Estimated effect: reduces effective concurrency in us-east-1 by ~18% within 45s of activation.
2) Model variant fallback: promote the quantized-v2 endpoint for the top-3 heavy routes for Zenbridge. Command (internal):
   - rwctl traffic-update --account ZEN-3421 --route "search*" --target-region us-west-2 --weight 0.15 --safe-checks true
   - rwctl model-fallback --account ZEN-3421 --routes "search*,rank*" --variant quantized-v2
3) Short-term cache pin: pin hot KV prefixes for 30m to reduce cache churn.

Estimated timeline: siphon + fallback live in ~5 minutes after approval; monitoring window 15–30m to validate. Postmortem owners: Infra (David) + SRE (Irene).

I'll run the commands once Alex confirms allowlist/CIDR or signals OK in the bridge. Logs and a step checklist are attached (stitch-playbook-v2.pdf).

David Kim
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

(Attached: stitch-playbook-v2.pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting requests (region: us-east-1)

Team —

Thank you for the quick coordination. Summary for execs and the customer:
- What we did: 15% traffic siphon to us-west-2; promoted quantized-v2 for heavy routes; pinned hot KV keys. Immediate 95/99 latency improved by ~40% and 5xx rate fell to ~0.6% in the diverted window.
- Current status: steadying but still monitoring for residual KV churn. Postmortem will include root cause analysis and changes to autoscale thresholds and KV pin heuristics.
- Customer support: Priyom — please offer a one-time goodwill credit (recommendation: 5% of last month invoice) and schedule an exec sync for tomorrow if Zenbridge wants a C-level readout.

Alex / Priya — please confirm whether the diversion caused any observed correctness regressions; if none we will proceed to gradually taper the siphon back over the next 2 hours.

I'll prepare the executive note and the extended remediation timeline for the postmortem. Great work.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
